title: He saw power.
paragraphs: And it made him feel dirty.
Peter wasn’t overwhelmed by the miracle.
He was undone by what it revealed about him.

Because when the nets broke under the weight of blessing…
his heart broke under the weight of truth.
“Depart from me, Lord, for I am a sinful man” (Luke 5:8).
Why would a man ask Jesus to leave… right after a breakthrough?
That’s the secret many won’t admit.

We say we want God to move.
We pray for miracles.
We ask for overflow.
But when His holiness actually touches our life…
…it exposes things we’ve been hiding even from ourselves.

The pride behind your prayers.
The quiet compromises no one knows.
The delayed obedience you justified.
The worship that looked alive… but was running on routine.
Like you love God… but something in you flinches when He gets too close?
Like you want Him… but not enough to fully surrender?
What are you secretly hoping Jesus doesn’t touch?

Because when holiness stands in your boat,
your self-image doesn’t survive.
Isaiah experienced the same thing. When he saw the Lord, high and lifted up, he didn’t celebrate—he cried, “Woe is me! I am undone… a man of unclean lips” (Isaiah 6:5).

Peter thought his sin disqualified him…
but it actually positioned him.

The very thing that made him say, “Leave me”…
was the very reason Jesus said, “Follow me.”
Because Jesus didn’t come for impressive people.
He said it plainly: “I have not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance” (Luke 5:32).
And repentance is not shame—it’s surrender.
But here’s where it cuts deep.

Some of us want Jesus as Savior…
without letting Him be Lord.
But not the fire that refines the fisherman.
And comfort never carried a cross.

If your version of Jesus never confronts your sin…
you may be following a version of yourself.
Peter fell down because he finally saw clearly.
And that’s where grace walked in.
Jesus didn’t say, “You’re right, stay away.”
Because the Gospel is not: “Fix yourself, then come.”
It is: “Come, and I will make you new.”
But Jesus stepped into that separation, took that condemnation on the cross, and rose again so that sinners like Peter… like you… like me… could be restored.
Saved by grace through faith—not by effort, not by image, not by pretending (Ephesians 2:8–9).
Jesus saw a fisher of men.
you see your weakness, your inconsistency, your hidden battles—
But Jesus sees someone He died to redeem.

You are not defined by the sin you’re trying to hide.
You are defined by the Savior who already saw it… and stayed.
You don’t have to clean yourself up first.
You don’t have to pretend anymore.

Because the same voice that exposed Peter…
is the same voice that called him forward.
If you feel that conviction right now—that weight in your chest—
Some scholars interpret Peter’s response as deep reverence mixed with fear, but what’s undeniable is this: Jesus did not leave. He transformed the moment into a calling.
And He wants to do the same with you.
If you’re ready to stop running…
“Jesus, don’t depart from me… change me.”
And next time, we’re going deeper into the moment Peter left everything behind… because that decision will confront your comfort.
We tell the stories that shame tried to erase.
